segments.text: Good evening. This is Zaka Shwani and I am Nishit Kumar with the news at nine.
The headlines.
President Rabdi Murmukh calls upon citizens to rise above personal interests and contribute to

In Badminton, PV Sindhu wins Women's Singles crown of Hylo Open in Germany, her second
title of the season and India bagged three silver and bronze at Swiss Open IWS Archery
Championship in Switzerland.
President Rob de Murma has said that every citizen has a responsibility to contribute
to social welfare and national development.
She called upon people to rise above personal interests and work for the larger good
of society and the nation. The president was addressing a function marking the centenary
of the sacrifice of Swami Shraddhanan at Gurukul in Haryana's Kurukshetra today. She
stressed that collective efforts are essential to achieving the goal of Vixit Bharat by
Highlighting the life of Swami Shraddhanand, the President said he worked for Social Harmony
and played an important role in India's freedom struggle.
Earlier in the day, President Murmur addressed the Haryana Day celebrations in Kurukshetra,
marking the 60th anniversary of the formation of the state.
She said the nationwide Beti Bachao Beti Padau campaign has proved to be an important milestone
in promoting women's empowerment.
She also said that Haryana had made remarkable progress of the past decade in various aspects
of women's empowerment.
Besides Haryana, several other states and union territories celebrated their formation
day-to-day. These include Andhra Pradesh and Amananicka Baraalans, Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh,
Delhi, Karnataka, Kerala, Lakshadeep, Madhya Pradesh, Puduchari, Punjab, and Tamil Nadu.
The Vice President and the Prime Minister extended wishes to the people of these states
and union territories on the occasion. Union Home Minister Amit Shah today praised
the Chandigarh police for its courage and dedication in combating terrorism and maintaining
law and order. He was addressing the 60th Raising Day celebrations of the Chandigarh
police in the city today. The Home Minister said the Chandigarh Police had displayed exceptional
courage during the era of terrorism. On the occasion, Mr. Shah conferred the prestigious
President's Police Color on the force. The Honour was approved by President Rob De
Murmoo. He also presented the President's Medal to officers and personnel of the
Chandigarh Police.
The President has conferred the President's Color to Chandigarh Police today. This
honor is a recognition of six decades of service, dedication and sensitivity. When the country
witnessed an era of terrorism, Chandigarh was not left untouched by it. During those challenging times,
Chandigarh police demonstrated exceptional courage and weller. Through its dedicated service
and commitment to good governance, Chandigarh police has played a significant role in protecting
not only Chandigarh, but the entire region from terrorism.
The Home Minister also flagged off 141 new vehicles for Chandigarh police.
Later, Mitr Shah inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for several development projects worth
258 crore rupees in Chandigarh.
Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit outlined his top priorities to strengthen and modernize
the Indian Air Force a day after taking charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff.
In his first address today, Indian Air Force Chief Cohen, the guiding theme VAU, articulating
four distinct pillars that will shape the IAF's future trajectory.
These are vigilance, victory and readiness, self-reliance, yukti, and unity of effort.
Through the VAU vision, Air Chief Marshal Dixit articulated a clear direction for
and operationally ready, technologically advanced, self-reliant and seamlessly integrated Indian
Air Force.
He emphasized on maintaining the highest state of operational preparedness across all formations
while restoring combat strength to sanction levels is a top priority.
Our priority shall be summed up in one word, VU.
In VU, V is for vigilance, victory and readiness.
Every squadron, every radar, every air defense unit and all the units along with each and
every air warrior must be ready to respond at a movement's notice.
Restoring our combat strength towards the sanctioned levels will also be my foremost
task.
A is for Aad Nirbharta, the Tejas Mark 1A and 2 the AMCA, Indian sensors, Indian weapons
are our highest priority. We will fight with Indian solutions and we will hold them in
numbers and to meet sustained operational demands.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.

Welcome back to the news at 9.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has hailed the inauguration of the Bengaluru Mumbai-Vandey
Bharat Sleeper train which was flagged off by Railway Minister Ashwini Vaish now today.
In a social media post, Mr. Modi said that the Vandey Bharat Sleeper train will be a game
changer for connectivity between Bengaluru and Mumbai.
The Prime Minister added that this train will benefit Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and
Maharashtra especially benefiting youngsters, IT professionals and students.
The train will cover the journey between the two cities in around 16 hours.
A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal today intensified into a cyclone named as Murasu
prompting Udisha and Andhra Pradesh to step up preparedness for another high intensity
storm in less than a week.
According to the India Meteorological Department IMD, the latest storm is very likely to
intensify into a severe cyclonic storm tomorrow morning.
It is likely to cross south Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm between
tomorrow midnight to early hours of Tuesday, with wind speeds of 100-100 km dusting to
120 km per hour.
The IMD has issued a red color warning for extremely heavy rainfall over coastal Andhra
Pradesh tomorrow.
An orange alert has been issued for Raial Seema, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Kharai Kaalan,
Thalingana tomorrow.
Heavy rainfall is also expected over Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Mahi, Odisha and South interior
Karnataka during the next two days.
Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh is on high alert with the state governments stepping up precautionary
measures to tackle the emerging threat via more from our correspondent.
The deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclonic Storm Murasu.
It is moving west-northwestward towards the Andhra Pradesh coast and is likely to intensify
into a severe Cyclonic Storm by tomorrow morning.
It is expected to cross the coast between Nellore and Narsapur during the early hours
of Wednesday with wind speeds of 100 to 110 km per hour.
Chief Minister and Chandra Babunidhu revealed the preparedness and directed departments
to coordinate rescue and relief operations.
Six NDRF and seven HDRF teams have been deployed, control rooms have been set up, and evacuation
of people from unsafe areas have been ordered.
People have been urged to follow official warnings and to contact 212 or 1070 for emergencies.
Ali Murli, Akashwani News, Vijay Vada.
Odisha is also preparing for another cyclonic storm, even as thousands of families continue
to grapple with the damage caused by Cyclone Ernab and the subsequent floods.
As a precautionary measure, authorities have also opened the gates of the Bali Mela Reservoir.
We have a report.
Southern Odisha still struggling to recover from the devastation caused by Cyclone Ernab
and the subsequent floods is brishing for another spell of heavier rainfall as Cyclone
next-term morass who approaches the neighboring Andhra Pradesh coast.
The India Meteorological Department has forecast rainfall activity in Odisha starting tomorrow,
with heavy to very heavy rainfall likely over southern districts on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandamal, Korapur, Navrangpur and Malkangiri are among the districts requiring
close attention, particularly vulnerable hilly areas and flood-prone villages, where
fresh rainfall could trigger flash floods and landslides.
The state government has identified vulnerable areas, particularly landslide-prone locations
and initiated the evacuation of people to safer places. District collectors of vulnerable
areas have been kept on high alert. Prakash Das Akashwani news, Bhubaneswar.
You are listening to the news at 9 on Akashwani.

Welcome back. Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the National Organ Transplant
games in New Delhi. Addressing Devan, the Vice President described the games as a celebration
of the resilience of transplant recipients and demonstrating the life-transforming power of
modern medicine.
Argan donation is truly a Mahadam, a supreme act of generosity through which hope can endure
even in the face of loss. Our Honourable Prime Minister Narendra Modiji has consistently
highlighted the importance of organ donation through his monkey bath addresses. These games are much
more than a sporting event. They recognize the dedication of transplant professionals and celebrate
the resilience of transplant recipients who continue to lead full and meaningful lives. On the
occasion Mr. Radhakrishnan witnessed an attempt to set a world record featuring 570 transplant
Transplant recipients and donors performing Tarasana together. Following the successful
attempt, the organizers were presented with a certificate by the World Book of Records
New Delhi for the largest congregation of transplant recipients and donors performing
Tarasana.
The country's gross goods and services tax GST collections grew nearly 23% year on
year, to over 231,000 crore rupees in October this year. It was driven by robust domestic
economic activity and a sharp rise in tax revenue from imports.
The center has withdrawn the special additional excise duty on petrol exports while increasing
export levies on diesel and aviation turbine fuel ATF.
Under the revised rates, petrol exports will attract no export duty compared to the earlier
levy of Rs. 250 per litre.
The export duty on diesel has been increased from Rs. 8.50 to Rs. 11.50 per litre while
the levy on ATF has been raised from Rs. 10.50 to Rs. 11 per litre.
In badminton, two-time Olympic medalist Piwi Sindhu has clinched the women's singles title
of Hilo Open, Super 500 tournament in Germany today, her second title of the season.
World No. 8 Sindhu defeated Denmark's Lion Hormak Kjarsfeldt, 21-12, 21-14 in the final
earlier this year.
Sindhu made history by winning the Japan Open.
Meanwhile, in the men's singles final, Lakshmi Singh will take on Indonesia's
Jonathan Christie in a short while.
In archery, India has won four medals at the ongoing SIS Open IWS archery championship.
Sachin Chai Chi, Tanya Rani and Priya Gurjeev claim silver medals, while Aditya Vadawa secured
bronze, Sachin won silver in the compound under 21 men's category after narrowly losing
the final to Germany's Simon Moritz by 145-147.
In the compound under 21 women's category, Tanya Rani also claims silver.
Meanwhile, Priya Gurjeev secured another silver medal in the compound women's category.
In the recurve, under-21 men's category, Aditya Wadhwa claims bronze.
In men's cricket, New Zealand defeated India by seven wickets in the fifth in the final
T20 international in Hamilton.
Despite the defeat, India won the five-match series 3-2.
The men in blue won the first three matches.
However, New Zealand made a strong comeback by winning the final two games.
